topics.name: Neural Networks
topics.description: Fundamental structures that mimic the way human brains operate to process data.

sub_topics.name: Artificial Neural Network
sub_topics.description: A computational model based on the structure and functions of biological neural networks.

sub_topics.name: Neural Classification
sub_topics.description: The process of categorizing data using neural network architectures.

sub_topics.name: Deep Learning
sub_topics.description: A subset of machine learning that uses multi-layered neural networks for complex data representation.

summary.prerequisites_summary: Basic understanding of linear algebra and calculus, familiarity with programming concepts.
common_misconceptions: Neural networks can learn without data
More layers always mean better performance

topics.name: Backpropagation
topics.description: A key algorithm for training neural networks by minimizing the error through gradient descent.

sub_topics.name: Gradient Computation
sub_topics.description: The process of calculating the gradient of the loss function with respect to the model parameters.

sub_topics.name: Gradient Checking
sub_topics.description: A technique to verify the correctness of the gradient computation.

sub_topics.name: Backpropagation Software
sub_topics.description: Tools and libraries that implement backpropagation algorithms for training models.

summary.prerequisites_summary: Basic understanding of calculus, linear algebra, and neural networks.
common_misconceptions: Backpropagation is the same as training a neural network.
It only works for feedforward networks.

topics.name: Activation Functions
topics.description: Functions that determine the output of a neural network node given an input or set of inputs.

sub_topics.name: Sigmoid Function
sub_topics.description: An activation function that maps any real-valued number into a value between 0 and 1.

sub_topics.name: Tanh Function
sub_topics.description: An activation function that maps values to a range between -1 and 1.

sub_topics.name: Softmax Classifier
sub_topics.description: An activation function used in multi-class classification problems to convert logits into probabilities.

summary.prerequisites_summary: Basic understanding of neural networks and calculus.
common_misconceptions: Activation functions are only used in the output layer.
All activation functions are the same.

topics.name: Loss Functions
topics.description: Functions that measure how well a model's predictions match the actual data.

sub_topics.name: Cross Entropy
sub_topics.description: A loss function commonly used in classification tasks to quantify the difference between two probability distributions.

sub_topics.name: Entropy Loss
sub_topics.description: A measure of uncertainty in the predictions of a model.

summary.prerequisites_summary: Basic understanding of statistics and linear algebra.
common_misconceptions: Loss functions only measure accuracy.
All loss functions are the same.

topics.name: Gradient Descent
topics.description: An optimization algorithm used to minimize the loss function by iteratively adjusting model parameters.

sub_topics.name: Gradient Given
sub_topics.description: The calculated gradient used to update model parameters during training.

sub_topics.name: Computed Gradients
sub_topics.description: The gradients that are calculated during the training process.

summary.prerequisites_summary: Basic understanding of calculus and linear algebra.
common_misconceptions: Gradient descent always finds the global minimum.
A smaller learning rate is always better.

topics.name: Classification Techniques
topics.description: Methods used to categorize data into predefined classes.

sub_topics.name: Linear Classifier
sub_topics.description: A classifier that makes its predictions based on a linear predictor function.

sub_topics.name: Window Classification
sub_topics.description: A technique that classifies data based on a sliding window approach.

summary.prerequisites_summary: Basic understanding of statistics and programming.
common_misconceptions: Classification is only for binary outcomes
More features always improve model performance

topics.name: Gradient Flow
topics.description: The process of propagating gradients through the network during training.

sub_topics.name: Gradient Backpropagation
sub_topics.description: The method of propagating gradients backward through the network.

sub_topics.name: Backflow in Neural Networks
sub_topics.description: The reverse flow of gradients during the backpropagation process.

summary.prerequisites_summary: Basic understanding of calculus and neural networks.
common_misconceptions: Gradients are always positive
Gradient flow is the same as optimization

topics.name: Model Evaluation
topics.description: Techniques used to assess the performance of machine learning models.

sub_topics.name: Evaluate Word Vectors
sub_topics.description: Methods for assessing the quality of word embeddings.

sub_topics.name: Checking Implementation
sub_topics.description: Verifying the correctness of the model's implementation.

summary.prerequisites_summary: Basic understanding of machine learning concepts and statistics.
common_misconceptions: Accuracy is the only metric that matters.
Overfitting is not a concern if the accuracy is high.
Validation and testing are the same.
practical_applications: Selecting the best model for deployment

topics.name: Shape and Parameters
topics.description: Concepts related to the structure and configuration of neural networks.

sub_topics.name: Shape Parameters
sub_topics.description: Parameters that define the architecture of a neural network.

sub_topics.name: Shape Derivatives
sub_topics.description: Derivatives that describe how changes in shape parameters affect the output.

summary.prerequisites_summary: Basic understanding of neural networks and machine learning principles.
common_misconceptions: More layers always improve performance
All parameters are equally important
Shape of the network does not affect learning
